report.tagline: An AI answer engine that searches the web and gives you one cited answer, plus the Comet browser and Computer agent.
report.simpleSummary: Perplexity is like Google, but instead of ten blue links it reads the web for you and writes one answer with numbered sources you can click. You can ask follow-up questions like in a chat. It also makes Comet, a web browser with AI built in, and Computer, an agent that can do research and tasks for you. It is free to use, and makes money mostly from Pro and Max subscriptions and business plans.

overview.whatItDoes: Perplexity answers questions by searching the live web, reading the top pages and writing a short answer with citations. Pro users can pick which AI model answers (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok and others). Comet is a free AI browser that can summarise pages and do tasks. Computer is an agent that combines many AI models to run long research and work tasks.
howItWorks: Type or say a question; Perplexity searches the web and shows sources at the top.
It writes an answer with numbered citations, then suggests follow-up questions.
Pro Search and Deep Research run many searches and write long reports.
Perplexity routes each task to the model best at it, for example Claude for coding or Gemini for deep research.
Comet browser lets you ask questions about any page or have the assistant fill forms and shop.
Spaces let teams save research threads and files to share.
overview.valueProposition: Fast, trustworthy answers with sources you can check, so you spend less time clicking links and more time knowing.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Answers with numbered sources from the live web.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Trust is Perplexity's main difference from chatbots and from Google.

coreFeatures.whyItMatters: The main reason people pay for Pro.

businessModel.summary: Perplexity makes money mainly from subscriptions: Pro, Max and Enterprise plans. It also earns from its API, commerce, and a small ad business. It pays other companies for the AI models and computing it uses, so its margins depend on keeping those costs below what users pay.

revenueStreams.detail: Pro at $20 a month and Max at $200 a month for more Deep Research, Computer and Comet agent use.
Enterprise Pro and Max seats for companies like PayPal and Ramp.
Telecoms and device makers like Airtel and Samsung bundle Perplexity and pay or share revenue.
Developers pay to use Perplexity's search-grounded answers in their apps.
Sponsored follow-up questions and shopping; small so far.

businessModel.pricing: Free; Pro $20 a month or $200 a year; Max $200 a month; Enterprise Pro about $40 per seat a month; Comet browser free; Comet Plus about $5 a month, with most of it shared with publishers.
costDrivers: Paying OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and others for model use
Computing for search and agents, including a $750 million Azure deal
Free Pro offers through partners like Airtel
businessModel.unitEconomics: A Pro user pays $20 a month. Perplexity pays model makers for each answer; a heavy Deep Research or Computer user can cost $10 or more a month, a light user $1 to $3. So Perplexity keeps roughly $10 to $15 on a typical Pro user, less on heavy ones. That is why it added usage caps, which later led to a class action lawsuit. Free users and free Airtel Pro users cost money with no direct revenue. Rough estimates.

howTheyGetUsers: Telecom and device bundles: Airtel gave free Pro to its customers in India, and Samsung built Perplexity into the Galaxy S26
Comet browser as a free download that sets Perplexity as default search
Founder Aravind Srinivas's public profile on X and in the media
Share links of answers that spread on social media
Enterprise case studies from PayPal, Ramp and others
growth.moat: Perplexity does not own a top model, so its moat is product and speed: a trusted cited-answer format, routing between models, and distribution deals with Samsung and Airtel. This is a thin moat, since Google, ChatGPT and Gemini all now offer cited AI answers.

improvementIdeas.idea: Show a clear usage meter for Pro and Max features, with caps stated upfront
improvementIdeas.problem: Users and a lawsuit say caps were hidden.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Lower legal risk and fewer cancellations.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Paid churn and support tickets about limits

improvementIdeas.idea: Citation check: highlight the exact sentence in the source that backs each claim
improvementIdeas.problem: Citations sometimes do not support the answer.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More trust and fewer users re-searching on Google.

improvementIdeas.idea: Airtel 'keep Pro' offer: a lower rupee price for users whose free year ends
improvementIdeas.problem: Free Pro users in India may drop off when the offer ends.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Turn free partner users into paying users.

improvementIdeas.idea: Expand the publisher revenue share and show publisher logos on cited answers
improvementIdeas.problem: Publisher lawsuits and blocked crawlers threaten answer quality.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More licensed content and fewer legal fights.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Number of publisher partners and lawsuits

pmLessons: You can build a valuable product on top of other companies' models, but your costs and access depend on them.
A clear, simple promise ('answers with sources') can stand out in a crowded market.
Distribution deals bring users fast, but you must plan how to make them pay later.
Hidden limits destroy trust; be clear about what users get for their money.

interviewQuestions.question: How can Perplexity compete with Google, which now has AI Mode?
interviewQuestions.hint: Pick a segment where Perplexity wins (research, professionals). Explain the edge: citations, model choice, no clutter. Name one bet, like Comet, and a metric.

interviewQuestions.question: Perplexity got millions of free users through Airtel. How would you convert them to paid?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment by usage. Find the aha moment. Offer local pricing, reminders before the offer ends, and clear value. Track trial to paid conversion.

interviewQuestions.question: What should the north star metric be for Perplexity?
interviewQuestions.hint: Answers that end the search. Break into reach, frequency, quality and paid users. Add cost per answer as a guardrail.

interviewQuestions.question: Publishers are suing Perplexity. How would you design a fair publisher program?
interviewQuestions.hint: Map value for each side. Options: revenue share, traffic back, licensing. Measure publisher sign-ups and answer quality.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Perplexity build its own frontier model?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare cost and time versus routing other models. Consider margin, control and risk. Recommend a middle path like small in-house models for cheap tasks.
